issues.description: The problem text instructs that the SealSaloon 'stock' should be initialized in the constructor, but later requires that the 'stock' attribute be static (shared across instances). A static final field cannot be assigned in an instance constructor. The solution declares 'private static final Stock stock = new Stock();' initialized at declaration. This contradiction between 'initialize in constructor' and 'make static' will confuse students about where and how to initialize the stock field and may lead them to write code that does not compile (attempting to assign a static final in a constructor).
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the specification: either require a non-static final 'stock' that is initialized in the constructor, or require a static (shared) 'stock' and instruct students to initialize it at the point of declaration or in a static initializer. Update the problem statement to remove the instruction to initialize the static stock in the instance constructor (or change the static requirement if the intent is instance-scoped).

issues.description: The problem specification and UML refer to a method named 'checkOrderReady()' that should be called after placing an order. The provided solution implements the same behavior in a method named 'processOrders()' and calls that from orderMeal(). This name/signature mismatch between the described API (checkOrderReady) and the solution implementation (processOrders) can confuse students about the required method name and expected API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across artifacts. Either rename the solution's 'processOrders()' to 'checkOrderReady()' (and keep its behavior), or update the problem statement and UML to require 'processOrders()' instead of 'checkOrderReady()'. Ensure the method signature and name match the API described in the problem statement so students implement the expected method.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML explicitly require a SealSaloon method named checkOrderReady() to process and serve queued orders. In the solution implementation the method is named processOrders() (SealSaloon.processOrders), creating an identifier mismatch for the same conceptual operation (serving orders). This inconsistency can confuse students when mapping the requirement (checkOrderReady) to the provided/expected implementation (processOrders) and when writing their own SealSaloon class to match the specification and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution method processOrders() to checkOrderReady() (and update all internal calls accordingly), or update the problem statement/UML to require processOrders(). Maintain a single consistent method name across problem, template, and solution (preferably checkOrderReady() to match the UML).
